ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the three-dimensional coordinate axes intersect at the origin, the z axis points upward, the y axis points to the right, and the x axis slants down to the left. There is a horizontal wire above, located in the y-z plane and parallel to the y axis, with the current arrow pointing to the right, i.e. along the +y direction; the origin is below this wire relative to it, i.e. the shortest displacement from the wire to the origin is along the -z direction. The slanted wire below is located in the x-y plane and parallel to the x axis, with the current arrow along the lower-left direction, i.e. along the +x direction; the origin is in the -y direction relative to this wire. Reasoning: The magnetic field direction of a long straight wire at a point is determined by the cross product of the current direction and the radial displacement direction from the wire to that point. For the y-parallel wire, the direction is +ŷ × (-ẑ), so the magnetic field is along the x-axis direction, and therefore the x component is nonzero. For the x-parallel wire, the direction is +x̂ × (-ŷ), so the magnetic field is along the z-axis direction, and therefore the z component is nonzero. Neither contribution is along the y axis, therefore the resultant magnetic field has no y component.

raw_record.question_text: Two infinitely long wires carrying current are as shown in the figure. One wire is in the y-z plane and parallel to the y-axis. The other wire is in the x-y plane and parallel to the x-axis. Which components of the resulting magnetic field are non-zero at the origin?

method.method_draft: First describe the visual geometry: identify the current direction of each wire and the shortest displacement from that wire to the origin. For the y-parallel wire, the origin is below it in the -z direction, so use \(+\hat y \times (-\hat z)\) to get an x-directed field. For the x-parallel wire, the origin is toward -y from the wire, so use \(+\hat x \times (-\hat y)\) to get a z-directed field. Since the two contributions are along x and z and no contribution points along y, report the nonzero components as x and z.
